subject: general
question: A retailer bought 50 kg of Arhar Dal at a discount of 20% Another 2 kg of Arhar dal was offered to him for free by the wholesaler on the purchase of 50 kg of the dal. If the retailer sells the entire quantity of the dal at the marked price to a customer, what is the profit percentage gained by the retailer?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Marked Price (MP)** is ₹1/kg.

Total Quantity received = 50 + 2 = 52 kg. Total **Selling Price (SP)** = 52 × 1 = ₹52.

**Cost Price (CP)** for 50 kg at 20% discount = 50 × 0.8 = ₹40.

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100 = [(52 − 40) ÷ 40] × 100 = (12 ÷ 40) × 100 = 30%.

**∴ The correct answer is 30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ad0afe36b778ae761a0860e1c658f16b1928eecb52adb36f40ab11fb41737d92.png] 

**Given:**

Quantity purchased = **50 kg**

Discount on purchase = **20%**

Free quantity = **2 kg**

Selling Price = **Marked Price (MP)**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Marked Price (MP)** of 1 kg dal = ₹100

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** of 50 kg dal = 50 × 100 × (100 − 20)/100 = 50 × 80 = ₹4000

⇒ Total quantity with retailer = 50 + 2 = **52 kg**

⇒ **Total Selling Price (SP)** = 52 × 100 = ₹5200

⇒ Total Profit = SP − CP = 5200 − 4000 = ₹1200

⇒ Profit % = (Total Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1200 ÷ 4000) × 100 = 30%

**∴ The correct answer is 30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Buy X Get Y Free Discount

Effective Discount % = [Free Items ÷ Total Items (Paid + Free)] × 100.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁ and d₂ are given, the single equivalent discount is (d₁ + d₂ − d₁×d₂/100)%.

Mark-up Percentage

Mark-up % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. It shows how much the price is increased above the cost price.
